# `security-requirement-added`

Auth now required, or an additional scheme

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `security-requirement-added` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Security ([RULES.md section 3](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An operation that needed no authentication now requires it, or an existing requirement now also needs an additional scheme.

## Why this default

Clients that send no credentials, or only the old ones, get 401/403 responses.

## Example

From test case [`security-requirement-added`](../../test/cases/security-requirement-added/): An operation that needed no auth now requires it.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
      get:
        operationId: listPets
+       security:
+       - apiKey: []
        responses:
          '200':
```

Findings:

- `security-requirement-added` · error · GET /pets

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  security-requirement-added: error
```

## How to fix

Make the new requirement an alternative (an extra entry in the `security` list) instead of a replacement, then remove the old one later.
